transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I keep cutting people off and jumping into their conversations at work, even when I tell myself to stop—I feel like I’m constantly intruding on others. It is starting to really strain my relationships with my colleagues, and I realized I finally need to figure out why I can't seem to control it.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others or blurting out answers before they've finished speaking, and does this happen in various settings, not just at work?

Yes, absolutely—I constantly interrupt people and even finish their sentences before they can finish, which has become a major issue during our staff meetings. It definitely happens outside of work too, especially at home with my wife, where I blurt out thoughts and disrupt her quiet time, causing a lot of tension between us.

Have you always been this way, or did this behavior start at some point, perhaps in childhood or more recently, and do you feel like you're doing it on purpose or is it more like you just can't help yourself?

Honestly, I’ve been like this since elementary school, when my teachers would constantly complain about me being too restless and blurting out answers, but it became much worse and highly disruptive about eight months ago when I started a new coaching role at work. I absolutely do not do this on purpose; even when I actively tell myself to stay quiet and let others finish, I feel like I just can't help but burst in.

Do you experience any other symptoms such as inattention, disorganization, or excessive fidgeting, especially since you were a child, or is it primarily the interrupting and blurting out that's been a long-standing issue for you?

I don't really struggle with disorganization or inattention, but physical restlessness and fidgeting have been huge issues for me since childhood. I'm constantly bouncing my knee, drumming my fingers, or needing to get up and pace because sitting still for long feels almost unbearable. Even in elementary school, my report cards always said I was too restless, couldn't stay in my seat, and kept tapping on my desk.
Have you ever felt like you have trouble waiting for your turn or standing in line, or do you often interrupt others during activities, not just conversations?

I haven't really noticed having trouble waiting in lines or interrupting people during physical activities. My struggles with interrupting are almost entirely centered around conversations, discussions, and meetings at work.

Can you tell me more about how you feel when you're in situations that require you to be quiet and still for a long time, such as in a meeting or during a movie, and do you find yourself getting restless or feeling like you're going to burst out with something to say?

Staying still in long meetings is almost unbearable and feels like my skin is crawling, which makes me constantly fidget, bounce my knee, or get up to pace. Even during quiet times at home, I can't stay calm and end up humming, tapping, or blurting out thoughts. In meetings, I feel this intense urge to speak and just burst in, cutting others off before I can stop myself.

Do you often feel excessively restless or have difficulty engaging in leisure activities quietly, such as reading or playing a quiet game, without feeling the need to get up and do something more active?

Yes, I really struggle to do anything quietly; when my wife wants to read or listen to music, I end up humming, tapping, or blurting out thoughts. She actually jokes that I'm like a wind-up toy because I'm constantly moving, pacing, or rearranging things around the house. Even on Sundays when I'm trying to relax and watch a game, I can't help but jump up to start some project.

Do you often feel like you're driven by a motor, or like you're constantly 'on the go,' even when you're not necessarily doing anything physical, and does this feeling of restlessness impact your ability to relax or focus on quiet activities?

I absolutely feel like I’m constantly "on the go," which makes it incredibly hard to just relax or do anything quietly. My wife actually compares me to a wind-up toy because I'm always pacing or starting projects even on weekends, and during quiet times I just can't sit still without tapping, humming, or blurting things out.
Can you describe how your symptoms have affected your daily life and relationships, and have you noticed any significant differences in the severity of your symptoms between childhood and adulthood?

My constant interrupting has caused tension with my wife, and at work, I've received formal complaints from colleagues and critical feedback from my principal, leaving me terrified of losing my coaching role. As a kid in elementary school, I was always restless and told to stay in my seat, but I managed to brush it off for decades. It's only over the last eight months in this desk-bound role that it has escalated into a severe, disruptive problem.
Have you experienced any significant symptoms of inattention, such as difficulty following instructions or making careless mistakes, in addition to your symptoms of hyperactivity and impulsivity?

I haven't really noticed or struggled with those kinds of inattention issues, like making careless mistakes or having trouble following instructions. My main struggles are really centered around the physical restlessness, pacing, and talking over others.

Can you think of any situations where you had trouble following through on instructions, or perhaps made mistakes due to not paying close attention to details, even if it seems unrelated to your current issues with interrupting and restlessness?

I honestly can't think of any times I've struggled with following instructions or paying attention to details. My difficulties have always been much more about my physical restlessness, needing to constantly move, and talking over people.
Have you ever found yourself easily distracted by your surroundings or struggled to focus on a single task for an extended period, even if it's something you're interested in?

No, I don't really struggle with being easily distracted or having trouble focusing on tasks, even for long periods. My main issues are definitely my physical restlessness, constantly needing to move, and interrupting others. It's the physical energy and blurting things out that I can't seem to control.
Are there any specific tasks or situations where you feel like your mind wanders or you have trouble sustaining focus, even if it's not as noticeable as your restlessness or interrupting behaviors?

I don't really struggle with mind-wandering or sustaining focus on tasks. My difficulties are strictly related to my physical restlessness, my constant need to move, and my tendency to interrupt others.
Can you describe any instances where you had to sit still and be quiet for a prolonged period, such as in a meeting or a quiet classroom, and how you felt or what you did in those situations?

Sitting still in our long coaching meetings is incredibly difficult; after ten minutes, my skin starts crawling and I constantly fidget by bouncing my knee, drumming my fingers, and twisting my ring until colleagues edge their chairs away. To cope, I constantly make excuses to get up, like grabbing coffee or making copies, just so I can pace in the back of the room. It's almost impossible for me to just remain seated and quiet like everyone else.

Have you ever noticed any significant difficulties with organization, time management, or completing tasks, which might suggest issues with inattention, separate from your struggles with restlessness and interrupting others?

I haven't really noticed any significant issues with organization, time management, or completing my tasks. My struggles have always been strictly around my high energy, physical restlessness, and my tendency to interrupt others. Those are the only things that seem to cause me trouble.

You've mentioned significant issues with physical restlessness, interrupting others, and blurting out thoughts, but relatively few problems with inattention or disorganization; can you confirm whether you've ever experienced noticeable difficulties with tasks that require sustained mental effort, such as reading, puzzles, or complex problem-solving, which might suggest some level of inattention?

I haven't really noticed any difficulties with things like reading or tasks that require sustained mental effort. My mind handles those just fine; my main struggles are definitely the physical restlessness and constantly interrupting people.

Considering your lifelong history of restlessness, interrupting, and now significant problems in your professional and personal life, do you think your symptoms are more related to difficulties with controlling your impulses and physical activity, or do you also experience significant challenges with focusing, paying attention to details, or following through on instructions?

My struggles are almost entirely about physical restlessness, talking too much, and difficulty controlling my impulses, like interrupting and pacing. I don't really have any trouble with focusing, paying attention to details, or following instructions. My mind is always fully engaged, but my body and speech are constantly running on high gear.
Do you think your main problem is more about not being able to control your impulses and actions, or about having trouble paying attention and staying focused on what you're doing?

My main issue is definitely about controlling my impulses and physical actions rather than paying attention. I can hear and understand everything others are saying perfectly fine, but I just cannot stop myself from blurting things out, interrupting, or constantly moving and fidgeting.
Can you think of any situations where you were able to control your impulses and wait for your turn, or has this always been a significant challenge for you?

No, it has always been a major, lifelong challenge for me. Even when I consciously tell myself to wait and let others finish, I still find myself bursting in and interrupting. Looking back, this goes all the way back to elementary school, where my teachers constantly had to tell me to stop blurting out answers and stay quiet.

Can you think of any situations where you successfully controlled your impulses and waited for your turn without interrupting, or has this been a consistent challenge across different settings and throughout your life?

It has been a consistent, lifelong challenge across all areas of my life. Even when I consciously tell myself "Let them finish, Marco" at work, I still end up bursting in, and at home, I blurt out thoughts while my wife is just trying to relax. This is a lifelong pattern for me; even back in elementary school, I was constantly in trouble for blurting out answers and being too talkative.

Can you describe how your symptoms of interrupting and restlessness have impacted your daily life and relationships differently across various settings, such as at work versus at home, and have you noticed any significant variations in the severity of these symptoms over time?

At work, my interrupting and pacing have led to formal complaints from colleagues and critical feedback from my principal, making me terrified of losing my coaching role, while at home, it strains my marriage because my wife feels I'm always wound up and unable to sit quietly. While I've always been restless, these issues became severely disruptive about eight months ago when I transitioned into this coaching role, which demands long, formal meetings instead of the active, free-flowing classroom environment I thrived in for years.

You've mentioned significant challenges with impulsivity, such as interrupting and blurting out thoughts, but relatively fewer issues with inattention; can you think of any situations where you felt like you were able to control your impulses and focus on a task without getting distracted or restless?

Honestly, I can't think of many situations where I feel in control of those impulses or able to sit still. Even when I'm doing things I really enjoy, I feel like I'm constantly on the go and unable to just relax. It is like my body and my mouth are always running, no matter how hard I try to slow them down.
Can you think of any situations where you had to work on a task that required a lot of detail and attention, and if so, how did you manage to complete it without getting distracted or restless?

I honestly can't think of any specific situations or strategies where I managed that well. I generally struggle with staying still or focusing on quiet, detailed tasks anyway because of my constant restlessness. It's just not something I've ever been able to handle easily.
Do you think your difficulties are more related to not being able to control your impulses, such as interrupting and blurting out, or to problems with paying attention and staying focused on tasks?

My struggles are definitely more about impulse control and physical restlessness rather than any trouble with attention or focus. I find myself constantly blurting things out, interrupting others, and needing to move or pace even when I try my hardest to stop. Focusing on tasks has never really been the main issue for me.

Can you confirm whether your difficulties with interrupting and blurting out are significantly worse in situations where you're under stress or excited, versus when you're in more relaxed or routine situations?

I'm not entirely sure and haven't analyzed it that closely, but it seems to happen in both situations. It definitely gets bad during stressful, high-pressure meetings at work, but it also happens during relaxed moments at home when my wife and I are just trying to unwind.

Can you think of any times when you were able to sit quietly and focus on a task without interrupting or feeling the urge to move, perhaps when you were very interested in the activity or when it was a one-on-one setting?

I can't really think of any times when I could sit completely still and quiet. Even during activities I really enjoy, I feel like I am always on the go or constantly needing to fidget. It just feels like my body always has to be in motion, no matter what I'm doing.
